questions.question: : The first American settlers happened to live in the midst of perhaps the most exciting period in the history of the English language. Had the settlers gone a quarter of a century earlier, America might well have preserved those pre- vious forms, as it preserved many other archaisms. P • Similarly, thee and thou pronoun forms were also dying out. This was a time when 12,000 words were being added to the language. One such change which these first settlers had already adopted was to use the s form on verbs, saying has rather than hath, runs rather than runneth. questions.question: Sl: In 1984, two small clay tablets of vaguely rectangular shape were found in Tell Brak, Syria, dating from the fourth millennium BCE. S6: All our history begins with these two modest tablets as they are among the oldest examples of writing we know. One of the animals may have been a goat, in which case, the other probably was a sheep. Lying there were these simple, unimpressive objects, each bearing a few discrete markings : a small indentation near the top and some sort of stick-drawn aninial in the centre. R : The indentation, on the other hand, represents, according to archaeologists, the number ten. S : These two tablets were seen by an expert the year before the Gulf War, in an unostentatious display case in the Archaeological Museum of Baghdad.
questions.explanation: Official UPSC CDS Answer Key: Option (A) is the correct response for this item.

questions.question: Sl: For generations, the Balaraju pond remained the primary water source of Perakalapudi village in Guntur district of Andhra Pradesh. S6 : It was only after major restoration work was carried out to restore the pond's storage capacity that the community could return to its traditional livelihood. By the 2000s, decades of water mismanagement led to a rapid drop in the groundwater table as well. However, overexploitation caused the pond to shrink to half its original size and reduced its water storage capacity by 60 per cent. The pond, spread across 24 hec- tares, supported irigation, sus- tained the fishing community, met household needs and remained home to a wide variety of flora and fauna. S • As the pond disappeared, the households relied on groundwater to meet their daily needs.
questions.explanation: Official UPSC CDS Answer Key: Option (B) is the correct response for this item.

questions.question: Sl: While most people are com- fortable talking about colour, the concept of luminance — even though it is more fundamental — seems less familiar. S6: This is something the Impres- sionist artists were able to master and it gave a shimmering, lively quality to many of their paintings. For example, given two patches of grey, they can easily tell which is lighter. Q : As the artist and art teacher Josef Albers states, just as a musician should be able to distinguish between a higher tone and a lower tone, an artist should be able to distinguish between higher and lower light intensity between different colours. Artists, however, must learn to distinguish differences in lumi- nance, independent of colour. But given two patches of different colours, it is often difficult to make the same distinction.

questions.question: Sl : Wooden fumiture is durable and long-lasting, reducing the need for frequent replacement. S6: A still better and sustainable, though slow, way is to plant new trees to maintain the forest cover. Some of these negative impacts are deforestation and the loss of habitat for numerous species of Deforestation in turn disrupts water-cycles and accelerates the pace of climate change. However, its use causes several negative ecological impacts. One way of reducing the use of wood is to recycle it as much as possible.

questions.question: Sl: Circadian rhythm is a term used to refer to the physical, mental and behavioural changes an organism experiences over a 24-hour cycle. BFVS-F-GNE - A S6: Maintaining a good circadian rhythm through appropriate expo- sure to natural light, consistent sleep schedules and times of eating, and adequate physical exercise during the day can allow an organism to live a healthy life. P : Prolonged disruption, moreover, can cause long-term damages such as metabolic diseases, cardio- vascular problems, and mental health issues. Light and dark (daytime and night-time) have the biggest influence on these circadian rhythms. Circadian rhythms are also affected by food intake, stress, physical activity, social environ- ment and temperature. When any one or more than one of these cause the circadian rhythm to be disrupted, it can lead to sleep problems, drowsiness and poor focus.
questions.explanation: Official UPSC CDS Answer Key: Option (A) is the correct response for this item.

questions.question: Sl: All the different parts of our eye help us to see. S6 : These electrical signals then travel through the optic nerve to the brain which in turn converts these signals into the images we see. P : The iris, which is the coloured part of the eye, controls how much light the pupil lets in. Q : Next, light passes through the lens, the clear inner part of the eye, which focuses this light on the retina. R • First, light passes through the comea, the clear front layer of the eye, and enters the eye through an opening called the pupil. S • When it hits the retina, special cells called photoreceptors convert the light into electrical signals.
questions.explanation: Official UPSC CDS Answer Key: Option (B) is the correct response for this item.

questions.question: SI : Humans in colder climates first began wearing some form of sturdy foot covering at least 40,000 years ago. S6: Today, minimalistic barefoot shoes are becoming popular because they allow the wearer to feel the ground beneath their feet while still offering some protec- tion and support. P • Unfortunately, modern shoes have also had a negative impact on feet due to bad design such as a narrow toe box, difference in heel to toe drop, however slight, and stiff soles. Earlier skeletons had very robust little toes that could bend and grip surfaces. R These gradually evolved to become less substantial than the big toe because shoe-like coverings reduced the mechanical stress on them and made them weaker. The evidence for this comes from the study of changes in the structure of the toe bones of foot skeletons from that time.
questions.explanation: Official UPSC CDS Answer Key: Option (C) is the correct response for this item.

Passage As the new century begins, it is becoming evident to urban dwellers, whether in industrial or developing countries, that there is an immanent conflict between the automobile and the city. Urban air pollution, often from automobiles, claims millions of lives. Congestion also takes a direct economic toll in rising costs in time and the use of petrol. Another cost of cities that are devoted to cars is a psychological one, a deprivation of contact with the natural world — an "asphalt complex". There is a growing body of evidence that there is an innate human need for contact with nature. Both ecologists and psychologists have been aware of this for some time. Ecologists, led by Harvard University biologist E.O. Wilson, have formulated the "biophilia hypothesis", which argues that those who are deprived of contact with nature suffer psychologically and that this deprivation leads to a measurable decline in well-being. Meanwhile psychologists have coined their own term — ecopsychology — in which they make the same argument. questions.question: Sl : Drought is a continuous and lengthy period during which no significant rainfall is recorded during the rainy season. S6: In India, droughts are more frequent in the areas where the average annual rainfall is less than 60 cm and the variability of rainfall is over 20 per cent. options.d: doomed SRSU-F-ENG/60A Passage—II People do not understand the nature or ramifications of most educational changes. They become involved in change voluntarily or involuntarily and in either case experience ambivalence about its meanings, form, and consequences. I have implied that there are a number Of things at stake—changes in goals, skills, philosophy or beliefs, behaviour, etc. Subjectively these different aspects are experienced in a diffuse, incoherent manner. Change often is not conceived of as being multidimensional. Objectively, it is possible to clarify the meaning of an educational change by identifying and describing its separate dimensions. Ignorance of these dimensions explains a number of interesting phenomena in the field of educational changes : for example, why some people accept an innovation they do not understand; why some aspects of a change are implemented and others not; why strategies for change neglect certain essential components. The concept of objective reality is tricky. Reality is always defined by individuals and groups. But individuals and groups interact to produce social phenomena (constitutions, laws, policies, educational change programmes), which exist outside any given individual. There is also the danger that the objective reality is only the reflection of the producers of change and thus simply a glorified version of their subjective conceptions. We can reduce this problem by following the practice of posing double questions : "What is the existing conception of reality on a given issue?" Followed quickly by "says who?"

questions.question: Sl : Drought is a continuous and lengthy period during which no significant rainfall is recorded during the rainy season. S6: In India, droughts are more frequent in the areas where the average annual rainfall is less than 60 cm and the variability of rainfall is over 20 per cent. P • This definition however, does not apply to Mawsynram and Cherra- punji, where even one week recording less than 0•25 mm of rainfall may be considered as a drought period. In general, the areas recording less than 60 cm of rainfall annually and in which the variability of rainfall is more than 20 per cent are the drought prone areas in India In India, the Meteorological Department has defined drought as a period of at least 22 con- secutive days on none of which is there more than 025 mm of rainfall. Areas where the variability of rainfall varies between 20 to 60 per cent are the chronic drought prone areas.

options.d: doomed SRSU-F-ENG/60A Passage—II People do not understand the nature or ramifications of most educational changes. They become involved in change voluntarily or involuntarily and in either case experience ambivalence about its meanings, form, and consequences. I have implied that there are a number Of things at stake—changes in goals, skills, philosophy or beliefs, behaviour, etc. Subjectively these different aspects are experienced in a diffuse, incoherent manner. Change often is not conceived of as being multidimensional. Objectively, it is possible to clarify the meaning of an educational change by identifying and describing its separate dimensions. Ignorance of these dimensions explains a number of interesting phenomena in the field of educational changes : for example, why some people accept an innovation they do not understand; why some aspects of a change are implemented and others not; why strategies for change neglect certain essential components. The concept of objective reality is tricky. Reality is always defined by individuals and groups. But individuals and groups interact to produce social phenomena (constitutions, laws, policies, educational change programmes), which exist outside any given individual. There is also the danger that the objective reality is only the reflection of the producers of change and thus simply a glorified version of their subjective conceptions. questions.question: Sl: Circadian rhythm is a term used to refer to the physical, mental and behavioural changes an organism experiences over a 24-hour cycle. P : Prolonged disruption, moreover, can cause long-term damages such as metabolic diseases, cardio- vascular problems, and mental health issues.
